summary:
Turn 31 reviewed the clean C1 artifact, whose checker set now contains only in-scope predicates, and recorded why the open scope issue still cannot be resolved from this product.

State on entry. The fresh artifact 53a31b99347546f88506a16282d28af8 (the clean C1 check submitted last turn) executed and reported violated with the oracle correspondence unreviewed. The open issue ef6b54abce294555b31a3c9a6ca606ac still sits on the older C1 artifact 05dc6a36…, which contains the out-of-scope applied-state property.

Review judgement (checker_correspondence, no_issue_found). The three monitored properties are exactly the accepted C1 obligation: adoption at the resolution (adopted_committed false), the recoverer-versus-committed-peer comparison (vectors_match false), and agreement across the three replicas after the Commit broadcast (all_committed_match false). No monitor selects the applied-state event even though the harness still prints it, so the executed checker set matches the accepted scope rather than asserting anything outside it. The requirement, applicability, prerequisites, identity correlation, groundings and driven rounds are the reviewed ones, with InstanceSpace re-read after every delivery; the prepared committed record and the substituted trigger remain declared limitations and are unchanged. The alternative that the applied-state observation should be confirmable under C1 is answered by claim C3, which owns that proposition with its own reviewed check.

Why the resolution is still pending, and what remains. The validator requires a resolution to address an issue on the artifact under review, its lineage or its semantic dependencies; this fresh artifact has no previous-check lineage to the disputed one, and my earlier attempts (resolution on the C3 artifact, resolution on the disputed artifact without a changed component, a revise_check with an encoding revision, and a revise_check as an ordinary repair) were each refused with a specific mechanism requirement. The two routes that remain are an F2 semantic revision on the C1 claim's scope or a revision of the disputed artifact through a mechanism the validator accepts. This is bookkeeping about attribution only: the three confirmed claims (C1's in-scope properties, C2's stable-store record, C3's applied-state effect) are unaffected, and no requirement, premise or earlier observation was weakened.
